text:
Kevin Lankinen's season has become a question of confidence, and the numbers explain why. He's 1-8-0 with an .812 save percentage, and he has allowed 14.7 goals more than an average goalie would on the shots he faced (45 on 30.3 expected), 2nd percentile. Last season ended at -20.3 by our measure, so this is a long stretch, not a cold month. The soft ones are the sharpest problem: .909 on low-danger shots against a league .962.

He didn't play between Nov. 3 and Nov. 22. Head coach Manny Malhotra said he has "begun that process of just regaining his confidence," per TSN, and Thomas Drance raised a red flag about how Vancouver is handling him, as Vancouver Hockey Daily reported. Canucks Army has asked whether he can be traded at all, with the five-year extension he signed in 2025. His return on Sunday came in relief of Nikita Tolopilo, who had allowed four goals on 12 shots against Chicago, per The Athletic's Mark Lazerus. Lankinen gave up two in about 47 minutes, his first night above expected by our measure since Oct. 4. A small step, but one he needed.
headline: Kevin Lankinen is trying to find his game
